target.title: [codex] Use Executing for default progress label
target.body:
## Summary

This PR makes progress drafts useful in the middle lane users actually asked for:

- Users can see Codex-level commentary while still hiding tool calls.
- Default progress labels are neutral and professional instead of themed.
- Custom labels stay easy to maintain through the existing config system.
- Telegram/plain preview text no longer leaks raw Markdown underscores.

TLDR: Red lobster as a logo? Fine whatever. But nobody wants to talk to a lobster.

Fixes #94850.

## Why This Matters

Progress drafts are temporary mid-run status messages. They disappear when the final answer is delivered, so their job is to reduce uncertainty while an agent is working without turning the chat into a tool log.

The issue was not only that one label said `Lobstering`. The broader user need is control over what kind of progress is visible.

- Some users want no progress drafts.
- Some users want a simple neutral status.
- Some users want Codex commentary, but not command/tool details.
- Some users want both commentary and tool progress.
- Some users want their own house style without bloating the already-large main config.

This PR keeps those choices on the existing `streaming.progress` surface instead of adding another global config API.

## What Problem This Solves

Issue #94850 showed that progress drafts needed a clearer product contract, not just a single label rename. Users need a middle option where they can see useful Codex-level commentary during a run while still keeping command/tool details out of the temporary draft message.

The old behavior also made default labels feel too themed for broad usage, made the commentary-only setting hard to discover, and let Markdown styling leak into plain preview paths. This PR turns the feature into a configurable, neutral progress surface with documented defaults, documented customization, and channel-level proof for the raw preview regression.

## User-Facing Flow

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  A["Channel streaming.mode = progress"] --> B{"progress.commentary?"}
  B -- "false" --> C["Show neutral progress label"]
  B -- "true" --> D{"progress.toolProgress?"}
  D -- "true" --> E["Show commentary plus tool/task progress"]
  D -- "false" --> F["Show Codex commentary only; hide tool calls"]
  C --> G["Final answer delivery unchanged"]
  E --> G
  F --> G
```

## Customization Flow

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  A["~/.openclaw/progress-draft-preferences.json5"] --> B["$include from each channel's streaming.progress"]
  B --> C["progress.label or progress.labels"]
  C --> D["Draft heading selected by shared formatter"]
  D --> E["Telegram, Slack, Discord, Matrix, Mattermost, MS Teams"]
```

## What Changed And The Value

| Change | User value | Maintainer value | Proof |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Replaced themed defaults with neutral labels such as `Working`, `Reading`, `Checking`, `Running`, `Testing`, `Reviewing`, `Updating`, and `Finishing`. | New users get professional status text by default. No one sees whimsical labels unless they explicitly configure them. | One shared label pool keeps channel behavior consistent. | `progress-draft-compositor.test.ts`, `channel-streaming.test.ts` |
| Kept the existing config keys: `progress.commentary`, `progress.toolProgress`, `progress.label`, and `progress.labels`. | Users get the requested choice without learning a new root-level config shape. | Avoids a new `channels.defaults.streaming` API and keeps the blast radius small. | Docs plus existing config/runtime tests |
| Documented commentary-without-tools mode: `mode: "progress"`, `progress.commentary: true`, `progress.toolProgress: false`. | Users can see Codex-level narrative while keeping command/tool calls hidden. | Makes the already-supported independent switches discoverable and reduces support ambiguity. | `docs/concepts/progress-drafts.md`, Telegram dispatcher tests |
| Documented the hidden customization pattern using `$include`, for example `~/.openclaw/progress-draft-preferences.json5`. | Users can keep preferred terms in a small private file and reuse them across channels. | Uses the existing include loader instead of adding another config-file convention. | `docs/concepts/progress-drafts.md` |
| Store commentary progress as plain text instead of `_..._` Markdown wrappers. | Plain previews and fallback renderers do not show raw underscores. | Rich renderers can still style commentary from structured metadata instead of encoding style into stored text. | `progress-draft-compositor.test.ts`, `channel-streaming.test.ts` |
| Added Telegram fallback/plain preview coverage. | Telegram users do not see drafts like `_Checking recent context_` in raw preview paths. | Locks the screenshot regression at the channel boundary that exposed it. | `bot-message-dispatch.test.ts` |
| Updated channel UI hints and regenerated bundled metadata. | Config UIs explain that commentary is opt-in and `toolProgress: false` hides tooling. | Generated metadata stays aligned with the source hints. | `generate-bundled-channel-config-metadata.ts --check` |

## Concrete Config Example

Commentary without tool calls:

```json5
{
  channels: {
    telegram: {
      streaming: {
        mode: "progress",
        progress: {
          commentary: true,
          toolProgress: false,
        },
      },
    },
  },
}
```

Reusable hidden label preferences:

```json5
// ~/.openclaw/progress-draft-preferences.json5
{
  labels: ["Working", "Reading", "Checking", "Testing", "Finishing"],
}
```

```json5
{
  channels: {
    telegram: {
      streaming: {
        mode: "progress",
        progress: {
          $include: "~/.openclaw/progress-draft-preferences.json5",
          commentary: true,
          toolProgress: false,
        },
      },
    },
  },
}
```

## Non-Goals

- No new global `channels.defaults.streaming` API.
- No change to final answer delivery.
- No change to auth, runtime routing, or release behavior.
- No change to the fact that commentary remains opt-in.
- No change to support for custom `progress.label` and `progress.labels`.

## Real Behavior Proof

- **Behavior addressed:** progress drafts use neutral defaults; commentary remains opt-in; `toolProgress: false` hides tool/task lines while allowing configured commentary; Telegram rich fallback text does not expose raw `_Checking..._`.
- **Environment tested:** Lexar worktree `/Volumes/LEXAR/repos/worktrees/openclaw-pr-94859-progress-drafts`, rebased on `origin/main` `e878efe950`, PR head `52bedd12b5`.
- **Focused local checks:**
  - `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.channels.config.ts src/channels/progress-draft-compositor.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` -> `15 passed`
  - `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.plugin-sdk.config.ts src/plugin-sdk/channel-streaming.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` -> `29 passed`
  - `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.extension-telegram.config.ts extensions/telegram/src/bot-message-dispatch.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` -> `168 passed`
  - `node --import tsx scripts/generate-bundled-channel-config-metadata.ts --check` -> passed
  - `./node_modules/.bin/oxfmt --check --threads=1 <changed files>` -> passed
- **GitHub checks on `52bedd12b5`:** `71 SUCCESS`, `23 SKIPPED`, `1 NEUTRAL`, no failed or pending checks.
- **Review threads:** `total=0`, `currentActionable=0`, `outdated=0`.
- **Observed formatter result:** Telegram fallback text is `Shelling\n\n💬 Checking recent context`, not `Shelling\n\n_Checking recent context_`.

## Evidence

Focused local validation covered the shared compositor, channel streaming preferences, Telegram fallback formatting, generated channel-config metadata, and narrow formatting checks. GitHub Actions on PR head `52bedd12b5` reported `71 SUCCESS`, `23 SKIPPED`, and `1 NEUTRAL`, with no failed or pending checks before this body-only proof-policy rerun.

The PR also includes the specific regression evidence the issue asked for: commentary can be enabled with `progress.commentary: true` while tool/task lines stay hidden with `progress.toolProgress: false`, and Telegram fallback/plain preview text renders commentary without raw `_..._` Markdown wrappers.

## Validation Notes

- The plan's original `--runInBand` flag is not accepted by this repo's current Vitest CLI, so focused local runs used `--maxWorkers=1`.
- `pnpm config:channels:check` attempted dependency reconciliation because this short-lived worktree uses an ignored `node_modules` symlink; the underlying generated-metadata check was run directly and passed.
- A previous CI run on `e7412a41e4` had a `QA Smoke CI` timeout in `native-command-session-target`, which is outside the progress-draft surface. After refreshing to `52bedd12b5`, `QA Smoke CI` passed.
- A Mantis Telegram Desktop proof request has been posted for the remaining visible-proof gate: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/94859#issuecomment-4873660499
